title: Register a subject before typing any train under it

facts.note: Any edit to the subject registry, or to plan files that contain typed train:<subject>:<slug> entries.
Planner tasks that create, rename, type or register trains/subjects.

values: train:<subject>:<slug> typed (under a new or an existing subject)
facts.note: Diff-level observer must detect every newly typed or re-identified train and every registry entry change, then check registration, naming and uniqueness against plan/_subjects.yaml.
Validation runs at CONFIRM over the whole registry and all typed trains and is confirm-blocking, so pre-existing violations also fail.

values: subject is not a noun-led durable object
facts.note: Registration, kebab-case and duplicates are mechanically checkable once an observer exists; noun-led durable object vs verb/actor/theme/route/category/owner/program name needs judgement.

fires: A plan types train:<subject>:<slug> where <subject> is not in plan/_subjects.yaml
A plan types a new train under a subject that is already registered (naming and subject+slug uniqueness must still hold)
A planner adds, renames or edits an entry in plan/_subjects.yaml, independently of any train
A plan adds a second train with the same subject+slug as an existing typed train
A registry entry or typed train uses a subject that is not kebab-case, not noun-led, or is a verb, actor, theme, route, category, owner or program name
CONFIRM runs and the existing registry or typed trains already violate naming, registration or uniqueness
doesNotFire: Changes outside plan/ that neither touch plan/_subjects.yaml nor type, rename or reference train:<subject>:<slug> identities, outside the CONFIRM validation run

given: A plan contains a typed train train:<subject>:<slug> or a subject entry in plan/_subjects.yaml
when: the planner types or re-identifies a train, edits the subject registry, or the plan reaches CONFIRM
then: Ensure the <subject> exists in plan/_subjects.yaml before any train:<subject>:<slug> is typed under it.
prefer: Add the subject entry to plan/_subjects.yaml first, then type trains under it
Choose as subject the durable object the train changes, written as a kebab-case noun-led name (this naming is mandatory, see avoid[1])
Reuse an existing registered subject when the train changes the same durable object
avoid: Typing train:<subject>:<slug> under an unregistered subject

Any subject (registry entry or typed train) that is not ALL of: kebab-case, noun-led, and the durable object of the train's change. This is mandatory, not a preference; camelCase/snake_case/other non-kebab names fail, and a verb, an actor, a theme, a route, a category, an owner or a program name is never a valid subject
Duplicate subject entries in the registry (registry entries are unique-by-subject)
Two typed trains with the same subject+slug (typed trains are unique-by-subject+slug)
Leaving an existing misnamed or duplicated subject/identity in place because the current edit did not change it; CONFIRM validates the whole registry
why: A train's identity is its subject plus slug, so the subject must be a registered, durable noun and identities must be unique for every typed train to resolve to exactly one stable subject.
evidence: Every train:<subject>:<slug> in the plan has <subject> present in plan/_subjects.yaml
Every registry and typed-train subject is kebab-case, noun-led and the durable object of the train's change (not a verb, actor, theme, route, category, owner or program name)
No duplicate subject in the registry and no duplicate subject+slug among typed trains
On failure, evidence reports subject, slug and registry_status
verifier_detail: Validation family: coherence; template: registry_entries_coherent; variant: planner_subject_invariants; subject_kind: subject

Checks: subject kebab-case and noun-led, the durable object of a train's change (not verb/actor/theme/route/category/owner/program name); subject registered in plan/_subjects.yaml before first train typed under it; registry entries unique-by-subject; typed trains unique-by-subject+slug
audit: Source statement: A subject is a durable noun object registered in plan/_subjects.yaml before any train is typed under it; subjects are unique-by-subject and typed trains are unique-by-subject+slug.

splitSuggestion.then: Name every subject as a kebab-case, noun-led durable object (not a verb, actor, theme, route, category, owner or program name).
Keep registry entries unique-by-subject and typed trains unique-by-subject+slug.

additions.text: Source statement bundles three invariants (durable-noun naming, registration before first train, unique identity). Only registration-before-typing is kept in then; naming (mandatory prohibition in avoid[1]) and uniqueness (mandatory prohibitions in avoid[2], avoid[3]) remain enforced here via avoid/evidence/verifier_detail until the proposed separate conventions planner.subject.durable-noun and planner.subject.unique-identity exist.
additions.justification: Rule 2: one obligation in then; avoid entries keep the other source obligations mandatory.

additions.text: A train's identity is its subject plus slug, so the subject must be a registered, durable noun and identities must be unique for every typed train to resolve to exactly one stable subject.
additions.justification: Source has no explicit rationale; this is a planner-facing paraphrase derived from the train:<subject>:<slug> form and the unique_identity term, not a new obligation.

additions.text: Reuse an existing registered subject when the train changes the same durable object
additions.justification: Direct consequence of unique-by-subject; guides toward compliance without adding a new obligation.

additions.text: camelCase/snake_case/other non-kebab names fail (wording in avoid[1])
additions.justification: Clarifies that the source's kebab-case requirement is a general prohibition and that the listed excluded types are not the only failures; no new obligation beyond S008.

additions.text: Leaving an existing misnamed or duplicated subject/identity in place because the current edit did not change it; CONFIRM validates the whole registry
additions.justification: Makes explicit that the source invariants apply to all registry entries and typed trains, not just newly introduced ones (validator checks the repo registry at CONFIRM).
Required by schema; derived from the source terms and validation phase.

avoid[1] prohibits every subject that is not kebab-case, noun-led and the durable object of the train's change, including the listed excluded types.
